opts: A uterotonic first, then gentle curettage; vigorous curettage risks Asherman syndrome
Immediate hysterectomy, since a uterus that has failed to involute never recovers
Antibiotics alone, because subinvolution is always caused by occult endometritis
Methotrexate to dissolve the retained trophoblast, then a repeat scan in two weeks
exp: A uterotonic is the drug of choice, with gentle curettage for suspected retained tissue; over-zealous curettage causes intrauterine adhesions.

opts: A previous infant with GBS sepsis, GBS bacteriuria this pregnancy, or a positive screening swab
Preterm labour alone, whatever the screening result or the previous obstetric history
Intrapartum fever alone, even with a negative screen and no other risk factor
Rupture of membranes for twelve hours alone, with no other risk factor present
exp: A previous affected infant, bacteriuria in this pregnancy or a positive swab all justify prophylaxis without screening.

opts: Not used in active management; tranexamic acid 1 g is added only when the risk of PPH is high
Both are first-line drugs of active management of the third stage in every delivery
Both are used only for induction of labour and never in the third stage or PPH
Both are contraindicated in the management of established postpartum haemorrhage
exp: Prostaglandins are reserved for treating PPH rather than preventing it, and tranexamic acid is an adjunct where the risk is high.

opts: Less space, so cord compression with variable decelerations, then fetal distress and meconium passage
Hydramnios with cord prolapse once the membranes rupture spontaneously in labour
Uterine overdistension leading to rupture of a previously scarred uterus
An entirely normal cardiotocograph, since liquor volume does not affect the trace
exp: Falling liquor in a post-term pregnancy compresses the cord, giving variable decelerations, fetal distress and meconium-stained liquor.

opts: A vaginal delivery is attempted, the hand is pulled to rotate, obstructed labour with Bandl's ring follows, and caesarean is needed
The lie corrects spontaneously and internal podalic version delivers the fetus vaginally
Cord prolapse occurs first and forceps are applied to the after-coming head
The fetus converts to a breech, and breech extraction with decapitation is then performed
exp: Neglected shoulder presentation is iatrogenic: traction on the prolapsed hand obstructs labour, and delivery must be by caesarean.

opts: Shoulder dystocia, instrumental delivery, the after-coming head of a breech and a rigid perineum
Every primigravida, to shorten the second stage and protect the pelvic floor
Every preterm delivery, to reduce intracranial haemorrhage in the preterm baby
Every twin pregnancy routinely, whatever the presentation or progress of labour
exp: Episiotomy is a selective, not routine, procedure; the listed indications all need a rapid or atraumatic delivery.

opts: Placental-site trophoblastic tumour and epithelioid trophoblastic tumour
Manual vacuum aspiration and manual removal of the placenta
Ventricular septal defect and transposition of the great arteries
Haemolysis with elevated liver enzymes and acute fatty liver of pregnancy
exp: Besides invasive mole and choriocarcinoma, gestational trophoblastic neoplasia includes placental-site and epithelioid trophoblastic tumours.

opts: Induction and augmentation of labour, since rupturing the membranes invites cord prolapse
Epidural analgesia, which abolishes the urge to push and prevents descent
Continuous cardiotocography, which alarms and forces unnecessary intervention
An episiotomy, which risks extending into the anal sphincter during a breech birth
exp: An intact sac protects against cord prolapse in malpresentation, so induction and augmentation are avoided; analgesia and monitoring are not contraindications.

opts: Warm saline in an intrauterine catheter compresses the venous sinuses; the Bakri balloon holds up to 500 mL
Cold saline packing through a Foley catheter is the only mechanical option available
An air-filled balloon inflated to 2000 mL in a Bakri catheter tamponades the uterus
Gauze packing of the uterine cavity is the current standard first-line technique
exp: Intrauterine balloons tamponade by compressing the venous sinuses; the Bakri is filled with warm saline up to about 500 mL.

opts: Cervical dilatation, pooling of liquor, cord prolapse, and a high vaginal swab for culture
Cervical dilatation alone, since the rest is assessed later by ultrasound
Pooling of fluid alone, because a digital examination is still performed afterwards
Fetal presentation alone, since membrane status is decided from the history
exp: A sterile speculum examination avoids introducing infection while assessing dilatation, liquor, cord and taking a swab.

opts: With radiology: uterine artery embolisation if she is stable — without: stepwise devascularisation through to hysterectomy
With radiology: immediate hysterectomy — without: embolisation performed by the obstetric team
With radiology: internal iliac artery ligation — without: embolisation by interventional radiology
With radiology: uterine packing — without: immediate hysterectomy for every woman
exp: Embolisation suits the stable woman where interventional radiology exists; otherwise stepwise devascularisation ends in hysterectomy.

opts: A preterm fetus, intrauterine death with a macerated head, the after-coming head and face presentation
Maternal heart disease, pregnancy-induced hypertension and a previous caesarean scar
An occipito-anterior position with the head already on the pelvic floor at full dilatation
A multiparous woman with a previously normal vaginal delivery at term
exp: Vacuum-specific contraindications reflect scalp injury risk: prematurity, a macerated head, the after-coming head and malpresentation.

opts: Forceps: facial nerve palsy and corneal injury — vacuum: cephalhaematoma and subgaleal haemorrhage
Forceps: sixth nerve palsy and subgaleal bleed — vacuum: facial nerve palsy and corneal injury
Forceps: cephalhaematoma only — vacuum: corneal abrasion only
Forceps: subgaleal haemorrhage — vacuum: brachial plexus injury from the shoulders
exp: Forceps injure the face and skull base; the vacuum produces scalp injuries, notably cephalhaematoma and subgaleal haemorrhage.

opts: Successful: send her home to await labour — unsuccessful: a second attempt, else elective caesarean — fetal distress: stop and deliver
Successful: induce labour immediately — unsuccessful: caesarean section — fetal distress: continue the attempt
Successful: caesarean at 39 weeks — unsuccessful: retry later the same day — fetal distress: give oxytocin
Successful: send her home — unsuccessful: caesarean at 37 weeks — fetal distress: retry the version
exp: After a successful version the woman goes home to labour; a failed attempt is retried, and any fetal distress ends the procedure.

opts: Fingers over the baby's back rotate the trunk so the posterior shoulder comes forward and delivers
Traction on the groin to bring the breech down onto the pelvic floor
Pressure in the popliteal fossa to flex the knee and deliver the leg
Suprapubic pressure while the baby hangs by its own weight to deliver the head
exp: Lovset's manoeuvre rotates the trunk through 180 degrees so that first the posterior and then the anterior shoulder is released.

opts: Either a fetus too large or a pelvis too small for each other, in a pelvis that may itself be normal
A maternal pelvis that is always contracted, whatever the size or position of the fetus
A fetus that is always macrosomic, whatever the size of the maternal pelvis
An absolute bony abnormality of the maternal pelvis in every single case
exp: CPD is a relative mismatch between passenger and passage, so it can occur with a normal pelvis and a normal-sized baby.

opts: Fetal distress, chorioamnionitis, abruptio placentae and intrauterine death
Maternal request for delivery at 34 weeks without any medical indication
A post-dates pregnancy that has reached 41 weeks with no sign of labour
An uncomplicated twin pregnancy at 36 weeks with intact membranes
exp: Induction is avoided in preterm labour unless continuing the pregnancy is more dangerous than delivering, as with infection or distress.

opts: Slow progress, marked caput and moulding, arrest of labour and the signs of obstructed labour
Rapid progress with early engagement of the head in the pelvic cavity
Complete absence of moulding, with a head that stays freely ballottable above the brim
Early spontaneous delivery with no caput and a short, easy second stage
exp: Caput, moulding, slow progress and eventually obstructed labour with Bandl's ring are the clinical markers of disproportion.

opts: A prolonged dilute Russell viper venom time, kaolin clotting time and isolated raised aPTT
A raised glycated haemoglobin, which reflects the thrombotic tendency of the disease
A high serum bile acid concentration, which prolongs the phospholipid clotting tests
A shortened activated partial thromboplastin time with a normal prothrombin time
exp: Lupus anticoagulant is detected functionally: a prolonged phospholipid-dependent clotting time that does not correct on mixing.

opts: Intravenous drug abuse, an active herpes lesion on the breast and untreated pulmonary tuberculosis
Maternal HIV infection, hepatitis B carriage and recent COVID-19 infection
Mastitis, a breast abscess and engorgement in the first postpartum week
Iron deficiency anaemia, gestational diabetes and treated hypothyroidism
exp: Breastfeeding is encouraged in HIV on treatment, hepatitis B and mastitis; intravenous drug abuse, herpetic breast lesions and untreated TB are contraindications.

opts: Fetal tachycardia, a maternal white cell count of 15,000 or more, or pus from the internal os
Maternal bradycardia with a falling blood pressure and cold peripheries
Oligohydramnios with a reduced amniotic fluid index on the ultrasound scan
Meconium-stained liquor with a normal maternal temperature and pulse rate
exp: Presumptive chorioamnionitis is ruptured membranes with fever plus fetal tachycardia, maternal leucocytosis or purulent cervical discharge.

opts: GBS colonisation, intrapartum fever, or ruptured membranes for 18 hours or more
Routinely for every woman in preterm labour, whatever her colonisation status
Only after delivery, once the baby has been born and the cord has been clamped
Only when clinical chorioamnionitis is already established during labour
exp: Intrapartum antibiotics are given for GBS colonisation, intrapartum fever or prolonged rupture, not routinely to everyone.

opts: About 1000 mg: 300 mg for the fetus and placenta, 500 mg for red cell expansion and 200 mg excreted
About 300 mg: 100 mg for the fetus and placenta, 150 mg for red cell expansion and 50 mg excreted
About 2500 mg: 1000 mg for the fetus and placenta, 1200 mg for red cell expansion and 300 mg excreted
About 500 mg: 200 mg for the fetus and placenta, 250 mg for red cell expansion and 50 mg excreted
exp: The total extra requirement is about 1000 mg of elemental iron, and the breakdown matters when explaining why supplementation is needed.

opts: Preterm labour, preterm rupture, rupture for 18 hours or more, or intrapartum fever
Term labour alone with intact membranes and no other risk factor
An elective caesarean section before labour with the membranes intact
A post-term pregnancy that has gone beyond 41 completed weeks
exp: When the GBS status is unknown, prophylaxis is given on the basis of these clinical risk factors.

opts: Atonic PPH: look for retained products preventing contraction, then continue management of atony
Traumatic PPH: suture the cervical and vaginal lacerations under anaesthesia
Uterine inversion: replace the fundus back through the cervix under anaesthesia
Amniotic fluid embolism: transfer to intensive care for ventilatory support
exp: A uterus that contracts only while being massaged is atonic; the next step is to exclude retained tissue that is sustaining the atony.

opts: Grade 2 increta: villi within the myometrium — grade 3 percreta: villi reach the serosa or beyond
Grade 2 percreta: villi through the serosa — grade 3 increta: villi within the myometrium
Grade 2 accreta: villi lying on the myometrium — grade 3 increta: villi within the myometrium
Grade 2 involves the bladder — grade 3 is limited to the serosa of the uterus
exp: Grade 1 is accreta, grade 2 increta into the myometrium, and grade 3 percreta to the serosa, with 3b for bladder and 3c for other organs.

opts: Dark red, non-recurrent, with abdominal pain and a precipitating factor such as trauma or hypertension
Bright red and painless, recurring at intervals through the third trimester
Recurrent with completely free intervals and a soft non-tender uterus
Only after sexual intercourse, with no pain or uterine tenderness at all
exp: Abruption bleeds dark and often concealed, with pain and a trigger such as trauma or hypertension; previa is bright, painless and recurrent.

opts: Contractions plus a cervical length of 2 cm or less, dilatation of 3 cm or more, or a positive fetal fibronectin
Contractions plus cervical dilatation of 1 cm or more and nothing else
Contractions plus a fetal fibronectin of 10 ng per mL or more in cervicovaginal fluid
Contractions plus a Bishop score of 6 or more with a closed cervix
exp: The conventional definition adds an objective marker: a short cervix, advanced dilatation or a positive fibronectin test.

opts: About 500 g at one week, 300 g at two weeks and 100 g by four weeks
About 300 g at one week, 100 g at two weeks and 50 g by four weeks
About 750 g at one week, 500 g at two weeks and 300 g by four weeks
About 1000 g at one week, 500 g at two weeks and 100 g by four weeks
exp: The uterus halves to about 500 g in a week, is impalpable by two weeks at about 300 g, and completes involution at 100 g by four weeks.

opts: A term delivery: it is not listed after an ectopic pregnancy or after an abortion
An ectopic pregnancy, which is the antecedent unique to placental site trophoblastic tumour
An abortion, which is the usual antecedent for placental site trophoblastic tumour
None of these, since placental site trophoblastic tumour has no antecedent pregnancy
exp: Placental site trophoblastic tumour characteristically follows a term pregnancy, with a long latency and only modest hCG secretion.
